recipes.name: Merritt’s Butternut Squash Gratin
ingredients_raw: 1 (2 1/2 pound) butternut squash - peeled, seeded, and cut into 3/4-inch chunks

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion and garlic in hot butter until onion is soft and golden brown, about 10 minutes. Add squash and brown sugar. Continue to cook and stir until squash begins to brown on the edges but is still somewhat firm in the center, about 10 minutes. Scrape mixture into the prepared baking dish; pour in chicken broth. Wrap the dish tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until liquid has been absorbed and squash is tender, 45 to 50 minutes.
Meanwhile, toss together Gruyère cheese, Cheddar cheese, bread crumbs, thyme, and rosemary in a medium bowl until well combined.
Uncover the dish and sprinkle evenly with Gruyère mixture. Sprinkle Parmesan cheese on top. Return to the oven and bake, uncovered, until topping is lightly crunchy and browned, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Merritt’s Butternut Squash Gratin
raw_recipe.description: This easy and delicious butternut squash gratin recipe features tender, sweet squash and a cheesy, herby bread crumb topping.

video.description: Your holiday table isn’t complete until you’ve brought this phenomenal and flavorful squash dish to share. Begin by adding chunks of butternut squash and some brown sugar to a skillet of sautéed onions and garlic. Cook until browned, then scrape into a baking dish with chicken broth. After baking until tender, mix a topping of Gruyere cheese, Cheddar cheese, bread crumbs, thyme and rosemary and sprinkle over the top. Bake uncovered until golden, crunchy and irresistible!

review.reviewBody: I have made this for 30 odd years. The 1st part can all be done on the stove top in a large saucepan. Just add the butternut along with the garlic and onions. Cook 5 min.,then add the stock,cover with lid. Bring to boil, reduce heat, simmer till tender.Remove lid turn up heat and reduce liquid till just moist. (don't let it burn). Put in baking dish and add topping. Just use tasty chedder and parm., cheese. The herbs over power the expensive cheese so why waste your money.

My husband and guest loved it! I used 3 cups thawed frozen, home grown, baked butternut squash. Sautéed onion and garlic in the butter, added thawed squash , brown sugar and heated throughout. Scraped the heated mixture into a 1 1/2 quart baking dish, topped with the cheese, bread crumbs and spices mixture. Baked until golden brown. Will definitely make again! No need to use chicken broth using baked and frozen squash

Amazing!! Made it exactly as the recipe stated the first time and it was delish....Tonight, I didn't have all the ingredients or the oven space. I made the onion/squash/sugar/garlic/stock mixture on the stove top and cooked until tender. Then I added chopped basil instead of rosemary. Cooked until almost all the liquid was out. When the oven freed up, I spread the mixture out on a small jelly roll pan and sprinkled with swiss cheese and italian bread crumbs and broiled for a few minutes. We ate all the squash and had leftover chicken. It's normally the veggie that is left over. A definite keeper as is or as a springboard for other variations.

Turned out well. I had to alter a little because I had frozen squash. But taking reviews into consideration I used way less broth (frozen was pretty soft and wet.... reviews stating how wet the dish was) and simmered it with the onion, garlic, herb mix till most of the liquid evaporated and the herbs were infused into what was leftover. Then added the squash and baked, covered for 20 minutes. Melted butter and mixed with bread crumbs and a fraction (don't like overly cheesy vegetables) of swiss cheese (that's what I had) for a crumb topping and broiled till brown. Turned out tasty for us. Will try with fresh squash but with less cheese, and maybe simmer the squash a bit in the broth with the herbs to help soften and lessen bake time. Will do again!

The recipe was delicious. I cooked the squash a bit longer in the skillet than anticipated, so I shortened the baking time to 20 minutes before adding the cheese mixture. Then, I put it back in the oven after adding the cheese mixture for another 20 minutes and it turned out perfect. Also, I substituted some shaved parmesan/romano cheese for the gruyere because I needed to use what I had on hand and it didn't hurt the recipe at all. It was delicious! I will definitely make this again!

This recipe was perfect for fall! I followed the advice of a fellow reviewer and did most of the cooking in the pan. I sautéed the onions and garlic then added the squash and brown sugar. I didn't have chicken stock so I used a pumpkin ale. I poured 1 cup into the pan, covered, and cooked for about 15 minutes, until the liquid was absorbed. I transferred the mixture to the baking pan and topped with the cheese, herbs, and breadcrumb mixture. I used a smoked gruyere and herbed breadcrumbs. After 15 minutes in the oven, it was done. So earthy and delicious! I served it with lamb chops and grilled asparagus. Thank you for this awesome recipe!

Great side dish for any day of the week.
My new fav 
I made a bit different by baking the butternut with olive oil first in the pan + foil for 40 min.
Then I browned it as written above and tossed with the cheese (only used the gryère), herbs, broth and bread crumbs.
Poured all of this in the pan again, no foil this time around.
Put it to "gratin" as mention above as well.
I cut about 20 min of cooking time this way.
Thank you for sharing it.

Way too much cheese - I reduced by half and it was perfect. This is a delicious recipe! 

I'm not big on rosemary so did thyme and Penzey's Fox Point, absolutely delicious. I also expedited the process by cooking the squash fully on the stovetop, mixing in half the cheese/breadcrumbs into the squash with some milk + boullion instead of broth, then put in a dish, topped with the rest of the cheese/breadcrumbs and baked til the top was crispy.

I just made it for the first time and it was quite good. I accidentally forgot about the chicken broth, but the squash was totally cooked and delicious I don't think it's really necessary. My store was also out of all fresh herbs so I used a little bit of Herbs de Provence that I had in the pantry. I used my cast iron skillet for the first half as that gives everything such an amazing flavor. Overall this turned out super well and I will make it again. I think next time I'll caramelize the onions rather than just brown them, and I'll double the amount of squash. this was a huge amount of cheese on top and it kind of overwhelmed the proportions of squash. Perhaps increase the bread crumbs by another half cup as well to increase the crunch.

I made this tonight and it was surprisingly good. I did (of course) make some changes. I'm just that kind of person. I cooked the squash completely stovetop, as I saw suggested, by first sautéing the onions, garlic, and squash, then adding the broth and cooking until the liquid was absorbed/reduced. I finished it up in the oven after putting in casserole dish and topping with cheese/breadcrumbs. I used about half the cheese called for, and I used whatever I had on hand, which was a cheddar blend. It still was very tasty. Will definitely keep in rotation.

This was delicious, BUT I used a round casserole dish instead of 9x13, and the cheese/breadcrumb mixture on the top ended up too thick and became kind of like a hard cracker on top of the squash. When I try this again, I will use a rectangle casserole dish in order to create a thinner layer, and I will take the advice of one of the other reviewers and mix half of the cheese/breadcrumb mixture in with the squash. I also used dried herbs instead of fresh because that's what I had, and the herbs really packed a LOT of punch. So if you're not a huge rosemary/thyme fan (or you're not sure if you are yet), I would say to reduce the amount you add, because the flavor of the herbs is quite powerful. I will definitely try this recipe again, even though it didn't come out perfectly.

This was a tasty recipe. The ratios of butternut squash to topping was way off. First, I could’ve used more butternut squash for the casserole, even if there wasn’t too much topping. I only used less than half of the topping and had to go and get more butternut squash to make another one to use up all the topping. It taste good, but I could never give five stars to a recipe that is this out of kilter.
I made this for Christmas. Very dissapointed. The squash itself was fine....the topping left alot to be desired. Very dry topping. Will NOT try again.
This is delicious! I cooked it as the other reviewer Clare Fisher suggested. So easy and less oven time. Next time I will double the recipe!

This is great! I've made it exactly as the recipe calls for- i've also mixed all sorts of squash, havarti instead of gruyere, Trader Joe's unexpected cheddar - you can't go wrong. I've also done dried herbs rather than fresh - its still great! However last time i made it I added crumbled sausage. OMG-it went from great to amazing!!!!
amazing! I will make this again and again!
I liked this recipe. I used different cheeses, using what I had.

This was a good recipe and one I might make again. It was not as sweet as most butternut squash recipes I am used to. The butternut squash really soaked up the chicken broth and it changes the flavor of the squash a lot. Still it was tasty and everyone in my house liked it.
This was amazing! I've served it at several large parties and there are never leftovers. Make it, you won't be disappointed!
I think it would have been good with some bacon bits!!
